items.title: Medical Director calls for accountability in healthcare delivery

original_payload.original_title: Medical Director calls for accountability in healthcare delivery
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Medical Director calls for accountability in healthcare delivery
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   4 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Kemi Akintokun
The Medical Director of Orile-Agege General Hospital, Lagos, Dr Temitope Bakare, has stressed the importance of clinical governance in ensuring safe, patient-centred and quality healthcare delivery.
Bakare said sustainable healthcare required accountable leadership, effective governance, empowered teams and a strong institutional culture of quality and safety.
She spoke at the hospital’s sixth annual strategic management retreat on Friday in Lagos.
The retreat was themed: “Clinical Governance as a Catalyst for Change: Positioning OAGH for Quality, Safety and Sustainable Healthcare Excellence”.
Bakare said the retreat was organised to review the hospital’s performance, consolidate achievements and set strategic priorities.
She identified accountability, clinical audit, risk management, patient safety, evidence-based practice and continuous quality improvement as key pillars of clinical governance.
“Our deliberations today are focused on strengthening clinical governance, which is vital to achieving safe, patient-centred care that is affordable and accessible in our facility.
“There is need to translate institutional priorities into measurable interventions that will improve patient outcomes, service efficiency and public confidence through clinical governance,” she said.
She called for a shift from individual efforts to institutional systems, departmental silos to collaboration, and identified challenges to measurable actions and sustainable results.
Bakare reaffirmed the hospital’s commitment to providing effective and affordable healthcare to patients.
Also, Dr Olufemi Omololu, Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Health Service Commission (HSC), said clinical governance went beyond establishing committees and policies.
Omololu, who delivered the keynote address, said it required effective systems to ensure that patients received the right care at the right time and in the right way.
“Healthcare excellence is not determined solely by infrastructure and equipment but by effective systems, teamwork and measurable improvements in patient outcomes,” he said.
He identified clinical effectiveness, patient and public involvement, risk management, clinical audit, staff management and development, education and training, and information management as pillars of clinical governance.
Omololu stressed the need for hospitals to establish effective incident-reporting systems, noting that reporting errors would help identify operational gaps and prevent their recurrence.
He urged healthcare workers to embrace a non-punitive reporting culture that allowed staff to report mistakes without fear of blame.
He also called for greater emphasis on measuring outcomes rather than activities, saying hospitals should provide evidence of how interventions improved patient care.
Dr Sola Pitan, Permanent Secretary of Lagos State Health District I, commended the hospital’s management for organising the retreat.
Pitan said clinical governance helped improve healthcare delivery through effective treatment and quality services.
He said strategic management retreats provided opportunities for institutional reflection, strategic alignment and renewed commitment to improved healthcare delivery.
“This retreat serves as an action-oriented platform for institutional reflection, strategic alignment and renewed commitment.
“When we engage leaders across various levels of hospitals, it promotes the democratisation of clinical governance and ultimately improves treatment and healthcare services for patients,” he said.
Pitan said the state government had continued to invest in healthcare facilities and supply equipment to strengthen service delivery across its districts.
He added that District I was implementing its Target Zero Initiative to eliminate maternal and neonatal deaths through collaboration among healthcare stakeholders.
The event was attended by Lagos State health sector leaders, including Dr Olusegun Ogboye, HSC Commissioner I, and other commissioners and directors of the commission. (NAN)
Edited by Folasade Adeniran

items.title: Diaspora investment requires trust, infrastructure, clear pathways – Experts

original_payload.original_title: Diaspora investment requires trust, infrastructure, clear pathways – Experts
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Diaspora investment requires trust, infrastructure, clear pathways – Experts
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   1 hour ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Glory Akpan
Experts in the creative industry have called for stronger investment infrastructure, transparent business operations and ownership of creative works to deepen diaspora participation in Africa’s economic development.
They made the call during a conversation session themed “Beyond Borders: The Diaspora’s Role in Shaping Africa’s Future” at the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 on Saturday in Lagos.
Timi Adeyeba, Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer of Amplify Africa, said lack of trust and clear investment pathways remained major obstacles to diaspora participation in African businesses.
Adeyeba said many Africans in the diaspora were interested in returning home to invest, establish partnerships and explore business opportunities but often lacked adequate information about the processes involved.
According to him, cultural connection and understanding should precede economic engagement, stressing that diaspora professionals needed to understand local markets, business structures and opportunities.
He said the media had also contributed to misconceptions about doing business in Africa, making it necessary for businesses and institutions to communicate their operations and investment opportunities more effectively.
Adeyeba cited interest generated by the Dangote Refinery’s initial public offering (IPO), saying thousands of diaspora investors expressed interest in participating.
He said the experience demonstrated that diaspora participation could increase when investment opportunities were credible and accessible.
Adeyeba, however, stressed that interest alone was insufficient without reliable financial platforms and structures that could translate inquiries into actual investments.
He urged African businesses to strengthen their operational systems and infrastructure to encourage investment and build lasting partnerships.
Jemilah Alghali, Senior Manager, Brand Marketing, BET Media Group, called for stronger ownership of African cultural products and intellectual property.
Alghali said African creatives needed to establish clearer cultural identities and standards to protect their works from external ownership.
She cited Caribbean dancehall as an example of a music culture supported by established structures and clear distinctions in its artistic identity.
According to her, African creatives should similarly define and own their cultural expressions to prevent others from controlling their narratives.
Timi Adeyeba also emphasised the need for indigenous distribution platforms to enable African creatives to earn more from their intellectual property.
He said dependence on foreign platforms and unfavourable licensing agreements could limit the financial benefits creators received from their works.
Temi Butler, Vice President and Deputy Creative Director, HarbourView Equity Partners, said African artistes should prioritise ownership from the beginning of their careers.
Butler said ownership could provide creatives with greater flexibility to license, sell portions of their catalogues and reinvest in new projects.
She said growing global interest in African music and emerging markets presented opportunities for artists and investors to establish stronger partnerships.
Butler also encouraged diaspora professionals to share expertise with creatives on the continent to support career development and industry growth.
She said meaningful collaboration required professionals to engage directly with local communities and exchange knowledge.
They also highlighted opportunities in short-form content, sports, digital media, film and music, urging African creatives to understand their industries and develop authentic stories capable of reaching international audiences.
They stressed that stronger institutions, transparent business structures and knowledge sharing would help transform diaspora cultural connections into sustainable economic participation. ( NAN )www.nannews.ng

items.title: Afreximbank pledges stronger financing for Africa’s creative economy

original_payload.original_title: Afreximbank pledges stronger financing for Africa’s creative economy
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Afreximbank pledges stronger financing for Africa’s creative economy
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   4 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Glory Akpan
The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) has pledged stronger financing for Africa’s creative economy, with a focus on strengthening production, distribution, branding and intellectual property ownership.
Dr George Elombi, President and Chairman of Afreximbank, made the commitment during his address at the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026, with theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, on Thursday in Lagos.
Elombi said African creatives had achieved global recognition through music, films, fashion, literature and visual arts, but the economic value generated by their works remained largely outside the continent.
According  to him, Africa’s creative economy is estimated at 60 billion dollars by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, representing only two per cent of the global creative economy.
He said tha African creators often generated successful creative products while foreign entities retained ownership of distribution platforms, branding, marketing channels, catalogues and intellectual property rights.
“Our talent is global, our share of the value, unfortunately, is only local,” he said.
Elombi said Afreximbank had increased its financing commitment to the creative industry from 500 million dollars to one billion dollars and subsequently to two billion dollars in 2024, following growing demand.
He said the bank was investing in the entire creative ecosystem, including production facilities, distribution platforms, branding, marketing, logistics and intellectual property.
The Afreximbank president said the institution had also established the Pan-African Film Fund for Production and Distribution to strengthen African ownership of creative content and expand its global reach.
He added that through CANEX, the bank was investing in African intellectual property, including films, music catalogues and musical compositions.
Elombi stressed the need for African creatives to protect and register their intellectual property, noting that registered rights could be valued and used to access financing.
“A right that is not on record cannot be financed and the royalty no one can audit cannot be priced,” he said.
He urged governments to increase investment in cultural infrastructure, training, studios and performance venues, warning against cuts to cultural budgets during periods of economic pressure.
Meanwhile, Creative Icon Richard Mofe-Damijo called for increased investment, stronger intellectual property protection and improved distribution networks to enable African creatives to retain greater economic value from their works.
Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, who made the call during his remarks, stressed that Africa needed to move beyond global recognition of its creative talents to building sustainable businesses and wealth.
He said African music, fashion, literature, films and visual arts had influenced the world, but the continent had yet to fully translate the influence into economic prosperity.
According to him, countries such as the U.S., South Korea and India had successfully leveraged their cultural industries to promote their identities, products, tourism and economic interests.
He said culture could influence global perceptions, consumer behaviour and tourism, adding that investment and strong institutions could transform cultural influence into economic power.
Mofe-Damijo said talent alone was insufficient to sustain creative industries, stressing the need for access to finance, intellectual property protection and reliable distribution networks.
He urged investors to finance creative businesses, policymakers to create enabling conditions for the sector and creatives to protect their works and build strategic partnerships.
The Icon said Africa must focus on ownership and wealth creation rather than merely being recognised globally for its creativity.
He said the continent had already demonstrated its creative influence and must now build industries capable of generating sustainable businesses, jobs and lasting economic wealth. ( NAN )www.nannews.ng
Edited by Vivian Ihechu

items.title: Tennis:Atilola wins maiden singles, doubles titles as Edwards stuns Ogunsakin

original_payload.original_title: Tennis:Atilola wins maiden singles, doubles titles as Edwards stuns Ogunsakin
original_payload.original_body:
Sports  Tennis:Atilola wins maiden singles, doubles titles as Edwards stuns Ogunsakin
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   5 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Vivian Ahanmisi
David Edwards stunned top seed Seyi Ogunsakin 6-4, 0-6, 6-2 to win the boys’ singles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 tournament in Ikeja.
Edwards recovered from losing the second set 0-6 to defeat Ogunsakin in a thrilling three-set final on Saturday.
The winner dominated the opening set 6-4 before Ogunsakin responded emphatically, taking the second set without dropping a game.
However, Edwards regained his composure in the deciding set, winning 6-2 to claim the title.
In the girls’ singles final, 13-year-old debutant Mofifunoluwa Atilola defeated eighth seed Bright Emmanuel 6-2, 6-1 to emerge champion.
Atilola displayed confidence, consistency and impressive shot selection to overcome her more highly seeded opponent in straight sets.
She controlled the opening set 6-2 before maintaining her dominance to secure the second 6-1.
The victory capped an impressive debut for Atilola, who expressed confidence in maintaining her form during the second leg.
In the girls’ doubles final, Goodnews Aina and Atilola defeated Adesewa Olaniyan and Gloria Samuel 6-4, 6-2.
Seyi Ogunsakin and Stanley Oriala claimed the boys’ doubles title, defeating Elisha Kwange and Gbolahan Olawale 6-4, 3-6, 13-11.
Speaking after her victory, Atilola described her performance as impressive, attributing her success to concentration and self-belief.
“My performance was very good. I stayed focused, remained in the game and believed in myself,” she said.
She expressed hope of sustaining her performance in the second leg, promising to give her best and remain committed to her game.
Atilola described the tournament as enjoyable and appreciated sponsors Procari Sweat, Peak and MTN for supporting the players.
She said their contributions helped competitors replenish their energy during matches.
The youngster urged organisers to sustain the competition, saying regular tournaments would enable Nigerian players to earn international ranking points at home.
“We need more tournaments like this so we can earn points in our home country,” she said.
Emmanuel expressed disappointment over her defeat, acknowledging Atilola’s improvement since their previous encounter.
“I feel bad because I beat her the first time, but she has improved,” she said.
She, however, promised to work harder ahead of the second leg scheduled for Nov. 9 to Nov. 14.
“I will train harder, study my game and work on other exercises to improve,” she added.
Edwards attributed his victory over the top seed to tactical discipline and adherence to his father’s instructions.
“I was strategic on the court and followed the game plan my father gave me,” he said.
He described the tournament as challenging but enjoyable, expressing optimism about improving his performance in the second leg.
Tournament coordinator Abimbola Okubewa praised the improvement in Nigerian players’ performances, particularly their dominance in the latter stages.
Okubewa, a former chairman of the Tennis Section of Ikoyi Club, said the competition offered young players opportunities to earn international ranking points.
He explained that such opportunities were essential for developing future professional players in Nigeria.
The organisers, he said, hoped to stage at least four or five similar tournaments annually to strengthen junior tennis development.
“This is the foundation for juniors to become professionals. They start picking up points here and gradually work towards becoming top-50 or top-100 players,” he said.
Comparing the current edition with the previous tournament, Okubewa said Nigerian players had made remarkable progress.
He noted that Europeans dominated the previous edition, while Nigerians featured prominently in this year’s semi-finals and finals.
“Last year, Europeans dominated the tournament, but this year, Nigerian players dominated the semi-finals and finals. The improvement has been immense,” he said.
Similarly, Matthew Holmes, a member of Lagos Country Club, called for regular junior tennis competitions to accelerate the development of young players.
Holmes described the first leg as successful, noting that it featured seven days of competitive matches involving Nigerian and European players.
He said regular tournaments would expose Nigerian youngsters to higher standards of competition.
“These tournaments need to happen regularly to expose young players to high-level competition,” he said.
Holmes also appealed to corporate organisations to support tennis development through increased investment.
“Corporate sponsors should come forward and invest in helping to develop Nigerian tennis,” he said.
The tournament attracted young players from nine countries, offering participants opportunities to compete for international ranking points.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the competition is being staged in two legs, with the first running from Nov. 2 to Nov. 7.
The second leg is scheduled for Nov. 9 to Nov. 14, with more matches expected during the six-day competition. (NAN)

items.title: Peace: I-G urges investment in security personnel, youths

original_payload.original_title: Peace: I-G urges investment in security personnel, youths
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Peace: I-G urges investment in security personnel, youths
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   9 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌‍‌‌​‍⁠⁠‍‍​
By Oluwatope Lawanson
The Inspector-General of Police (I-G), Mr Olatunji Disu, has called for more investments in the professional development of security personnel and youths to strengthen peace and security.
He also called for stronger partnership with Rotary International to strengthen community policing, promote conflict prevention and build safer communities across Nigeria.
Disu made the call at the All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit on Saturday in Ikeja.
The summit had the theme, “Good Governance, Justice and Equity: Foundations for Sustainable Peace”.
Disu was represented by Assistant Inspector-General of Police Miller Dantawaye in charge of Zone 13 Police Command.
The command comprises Anambra and Enugu states.
Disu stressed the need to invest in the professional development of security personnel and young people, describing such investments as essential to lasting peace and security.
He reaffirmed the commitment of the Nigeria Police Force to partnerships that would promote justice, responsible citizenship and peaceful communities.
The I-G said sustainable peace went beyond the absence of violence, stressing that it required justice, fairness, good governance, respect for human rights and institutions that would enjoy public confidence.
Disu said that equity and the rule of law were essential foundations for national stability.
According to him, citizens are more likely to resolve grievances through lawful and peaceful means when they believe that the law applies equally to everyone.
He said that equal protection, access to justice and respect for human dignity were necessary for building peaceful and stable communities.
He said the police remained committed to protecting lives and property, preventing and detecting crime, maintaining public order and enforcing law professionally and impartially.
The I-G, however, said that security was not the sole responsibility of the police, noting that effective policing required the cooperation and active participation of citizens.
He described community policing as an important bridge between law enforcement institutions and communities.
“Effective policing requires more than the presence of officers on our streets.
“It requires communication, cooperation, mutual respect and a shared understanding of the security challenges confronting our communities,” he said.
Disu said that citizens’ trust in the police would encourage them to provide useful information, report crimes and cooperate with investigations.
He added that police officers, who understood the concerns and realities of their communities, would be better positioned to prevent crimes and resolve disputes.
The I-G said that trust must be earned through professional conduct, transparency, accountability, responsiveness and respect for human rights.
He highlighted the role of Rotary International in promoting peacebuilding through its commitment to fellowship, integrity, diversity and service to humanity.
Disu said that there was considerable opportunity for the Nigeria Police Force and Rotary to develop partnerships in peace education, youth engagement, community dialogue, conflict prevention and public safety awareness.
He said Rotary International’s extensive community networks and the police’s nationwide presence could complement each other in identifying local security challenges, promoting responsible citizenship and encouraging peaceful resolution of disputes.
The I-G urged Rotary International to support qualified police officers to access its Peace Fellowship programmes to strengthen their expertise in conflict prevention, mediation, community engagement and peacebuilding.
He noted that the programmes provided specialised training in peacebuilding, conflict prevention and resolution, adding that such opportunities would improve the capacities of police personnel to manage security challenges.
Disu said that criminals continually adapted their strategies, making it necessary for the police to regularly improve their knowledge, skills and approaches to stay ahead of security threats.
He urged strengthening of partnerships between institutions and communities, governments and citizens, and security agencies and service organisations.(NAN)

items.title: Elections: Swedish envoy urges stronger democratic institutions, inclusive governance

original_payload.original_title: Elections: Swedish envoy urges stronger democratic institutions, inclusive governance
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Elections: Swedish envoy urges stronger democratic institutions, inclusive governance
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   7 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌‍‌‌​‍⁠
By Oluwatope Lawanson
Sweden has called for stronger democratic institutions, inclusive governance and sustained dialogue to promote lasting peace and peaceful elections in Nigeria.
Sweden’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Anna Westerholm, made the call at the All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit on Saturday in Ikeja.
The summit had the theme, “Good Governance, Justice and Equity: Foundations for Sustainable Peace”.
Westerholm said that peaceful elections depended on public confidence in institutions, sustained political dialogue and commitment to resolving differences without violence.
“Peaceful elections are not built on the election day.
“Peaceful elections are built on confidence in institutions, on sustained political dialogue, on a shared commitment to resolving differences without violence,” she said.
The envoy stressed the importance of women participation in peacebuilding.
According to her, women should not be regarded merely as victims of conflict but as active leaders in preventing violence and promoting peace.
She noted that women and children were particularly vulnerable to violence, displacement and insecurity during conflicts.
“Yet, women are far more than victims of conflict. There can be no lasting peace without our meaningful participation.
“We are not simply beneficiaries of peace, we are leaders in preventing conflicts and building peace,” she said.
Westerholm described inclusion as a fundamental requirement for sustainable peace.
She added that peacebuilding involved practical efforts by individuals and organisations committed to resolving disputes and preventing violence.
She commended the contributions of Peace Corps and Peace Activator Fellows, who, she said, helped to resolve disputes, bridge divides and prevent tensions from escalating into violence in their communities.
The ambassador said the summit’s theme was relevant, stressing that discussions on peace must translate into measurable outcomes.
She urged stakeholders developing commitments and peace legacy agenda at the summit to ensure that their declarations would contain clear actions, designated responsibilities and mechanisms for measuring progress.
“Do not measure success by the words of your communique.
“Measure it by safer communities, greater trust in institutions, peaceful elections, and young Nigerians who see opportunities to build their future here, at home,” she said.
Westerholm said that Sweden and Nigeria were marking 65 years of diplomatic relations, adding that development, security and peace remained interconnected throughout the relationship.
She said that Sweden’s approach to sustainable peace was anchored on democratic institutions, human rights, dialogue and economic opportunities.
According to her, Europe’s history and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war demonstrate the devastating consequences of conflict and the need for every generation to defend and renew peace.
“Peace is never guaranteed. It must be defended and renewed by every generation,” she said.
The ambassador emphasised that peace could not be achieved by governments, international organisations or security forces alone but by collective commitment of communities, civil societies, businesses and individuals.
She reaffirmed Sweden’s commitment to working with Nigeria to strengthen foundations of lasting peace.
“The question is no longer why peace matters. We know, of course, it does. The question is: What are we prepared to invest to sustain it?” she asked.
She urged participants to ensure that the summit would produce concrete results capable of contributing to a lasting peace legacy in Nigeria. (NAN)www.nannews.ng

items.title: UNIMAID VC tasks alumni on stronger support for university’s growth

original_payload.original_title: UNIMAID VC tasks alumni on stronger support for university’s growth
original_payload.original_body:
Education  UNIMAID VC tasks alumni on stronger support for university’s growth
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   15 minutes ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Hayatullah ​‌⁠⁠‌‌‍⁠⁠‍‍​​⁠‍‌‍‍‌​Idris
The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Maiduguri (UNIMAID), Prof. Muhammed Mele, has urged alumni of the institution to provide stronger financial, intellectual and professional support to sustain its growth and academic excellence.
Mele made the call at the university’s first Global Annual Reunion Dinner and Awards Night, organised by the UNIMAID Alumni Association in Abuja.
He said the university’s continued development required more than government intervention, adding that alumni must take greater responsibility for funding, institutional development and preservation of its legacy.
The vice-chancellor urged graduates, irrespective of their professional positions and locations, to reconnect with their alma mater and contribute meaningfully to its advancement.
“Let us build UNIMAID so that it can continue to strengthen our beloved nation, Nigeria,” he said.
Mele said the institution had produced graduates making significant contributions across government, corporate organisations, security agencies, educational institutions and international organisations.
He described the alumni as ambassadors of the institution’s values and academic tradition, adding that their achievements reflect the quality of education and training received at the university.
“Wherever our alumni go, they carry the touch of UNIMAID with them, and they do that with unmatched distinction,” he said.
He said the institution’s ability to withstand years of difficult circumstances, particularly the challenges of insurgency and insecurity in the North-East, demonstrated the importance of collective commitment to its survival and development.
Mele acknowledged the support of the Federal Government, President Bola Tinubu, who is the university’s Visitor, Borno Governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum, other state governors, members of the National Assembly, development partners and traditional rulers.
He, however, said that the alumni support remained essential to consolidating the gains recorded, and to sustaining the university’s pursuit of excellence.
The vice-chancellor also commended Vice-President Kashim Shettima for his leadership and contributions to national development, particularly his role in mobilising support for the successful relaunch of the university’s endowment fund.
Congratulating the award recipients, Mele urged the alumni to see the reunion as an opportunity to renew their commitment to the institution rather than merely reminisce about their university days.
“Let us see this night, not just as a night to wine and dine and remember our days on campus, but also a night for all of us to renew our sacred past,” he said.
Earlier, the Global President of the UNIMAID Alumni Association, Baba Shettima-Kukawa, said the association had registered nearly 10,000 graduates through its newly established online portal.
Shettima-Kukawa described the database as the largest assembly of the university’s alumni records in its history.
He said the digital platform had also enabled the association to conduct its first nationwide online election, covering the entire process from declaration of interest by aspirants to announcement of winners.
According to him, the initiative is part of efforts to build a transparent, inclusive and sustainable alumni structure capable of maintaining continuity despite changes in leadership.
He also said that the association was developing a scholarship endowment fund, mentorship programme and professional development board to support students and graduates.
He expressed optimism that the initiatives would become operational before the end of the year, saying they are designed to strengthen the relationship between the university and its graduates while creating opportunities for younger members.
In his keynote address, the President of the Worldwide University of Lagos Alumni Association, Ifeoluwa Oyedele, identified institutional resilience, leadership continuity and structured mentorship as critical to building effective alumni associations.
Oyedele described the UNIMAID Alumni Association as a community that creates lifelong relationships, shared values, and a common identity.
He commended UNIMAID for maintaining its presence in Maiduguri and sustaining academic activities despite the devastating effects of insurgency and insecurity in the North-East.
He said that its decision to remain open demonstrated the determination of its management, staff, students and alumni.
Oyedele said the university’s experience offered important lessons on resilience, institutional commitment and the need for alumni to support their institutions during periods of adversity.
He said that alumni associations risked losing institutional memory and developmental momentum without effective leadership succession arrangements.
He urged the association to establish structures that would guarantee continuity of programmes beyond the tenure of individual executives.
“There is a need for structured mentorship programmes to help younger graduates navigate unemployment, economic uncertainty and professional development challenges.
“Stronger connections between older graduates, undergraduates and current students will enable alumni associations to mobilise their collective intellectual, professional, financial and social resources for institutional advancement.
“Unity among alumni does not require uniformity of opinion; members can disagree on issues and still remain committed to a common institutional purpose,” he said.
The reunion had the theme, “Unity, Resilience and Impact: Building UNIMAID, Strengthening the Nation”.
It brought together graduates and other stakeholders to celebrate the university’s achievements, honour distinguished alumni and discuss strategies for strengthening its future. (NAN) www.nannews.ng

items.title: Five years of the Petroleum Industry Act

original_payload.original_title: Five years of the Petroleum Industry Act
original_payload.original_body:
By Chidi Anselm Odinkalu
When he ran for the office of president on the platform of the Peoples’ Democratic Party (PDP) in Nigeria’s 2019 general elections, Nigeria’s former Vice-President, Atiku Abubakar, famously promised to privatise Nigeria’s hydrocarbon and energy assets. Taking aim at the Nigeria National Petroleum Company (NNPC),  he argued  that “privatising NNPC would be to our advantage. We are not going to lose anything, but we will rather gain a lot.”
The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) at the time  mocked the idea , accusing him of harbouring an undisguised desire to dispose of the nation’s crown jewels to himself and his friends. Two and a half years later, in August 2021, President Muhammadu Buhari assented to the  Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) , substantially implementing the idea of de-regulating the hydrocarbons sector in the country and enacting a vision for transitioning Nigeria’s petroleum industry onto a globally competitive footing.
Five years after the adoption of the Act, this vision confronts a rapidly evolving global context in a domestic election season.
Comprising 319 sections and eight schedules, the PIA is one of the most complex pieces of legislation on the books in Nigeria. Most professionals, not to speak of less-informed citizens, will not read or access it.

items.title: Culture : Mawndoé Célestin invite les médias à repenser l’avenir de l’art au Tchad

original_payload.original_title: Culture : Mawndoé Célestin invite les médias à repenser l’avenir de l’art au Tchad
original_payload.original_body:
À l’occasion d’un déjeuner de presse organisé le samedi 7 novembre 2026 à l’Espace Au nom de l’art, à Bakara, l’artiste musicien Mawndoé Célestin a partagé ses réflexions sur les difficultés du secteur culturel tchadien. Au-delà de la présentation des activités de cet espace artistique, il a surtout appelé à une réflexion collective sur la structuration du marché de l’art et les conditions économiques permettant aux artistes de vivre de leur métier.
Pour Mawndoé Célestin, cette rencontre avec les professionnels des médias ne devait pas être un simple exercice de communication. Initialement envisagée comme un point de presse, puis rebaptisée déjeuner de presse, elle se voulait avant tout un moment d’échange autour des réalités du secteur culturel.
Combien d’artistes tchadiens parviennent réellement à vivre de leur art ? Et dans quels domaines ? Pour l’artiste, le débat culturel ne doit pas se limiter à la musique, souvent considérée comme la principale expression artistique. Il rappelle que les peintres, les sculpteurs, les comédiens et d’autres acteurs évoluent également dans cet univers, sans que l’existence d’un marché suffisamment structuré soit toujours garantie. Pour lui, la capacité des artistes à financer leur communication, à organiser des tournées nationales ou simplement à subvenir à leurs besoins dépend largement de la vitalité de ce marché. Selon lui, tant que les artistes ne pourront pas tirer des revenus suffisants de leurs créations, ils auront difficilement les moyens de rémunérer les autres acteurs qui contribuent à la promotion de leur travail.
L’éducation artistique comme point de départ
L’artiste a également insisté sur l’importance de l’éducation à l’art dès le plus jeune âge. À travers les Ateliers de Mawndoé, l’ambition est notamment de familiariser les enfants avec les différentes formes d’expression artistique et de leur permettre de développer un intérêt pour la création. Il estime que le rapport à l’art se construit dès l’enfance, à travers les expériences et les espaces fréquentés. À ses yeux, emmener régulièrement un enfant dans un musée ou lui donner accès à des activités artistiques peut contribuer à faire naître chez lui une vocation, mais aussi à former un futur public.
Pour concrétiser cette vision, l’Espace Au nom de l’art entend proposer un cadre accueillant différentes activités culturelles, artistiques et récréatives.  Des activités de karaté, de danse et d’animation y sont également proposées aux jeunes. Sur le plan économique, l’espace développe notamment des offres de team building, de restauration et des scènes ouvertes. Ces dernières permettent à des personnes qui sont habituellement éloignées des scènes artistiques de prendre le micro et de participer aux prestations.
Au-delà de la présentation de cet espace, l’artiste a invité les professionnels des médias à prendre part à une réflexion sur l’avenir de l’écosystème culturel tchadien. Il estime qu’il existe aujourd’hui une dynamique dans le milieu artistique, avec des créateurs qui commencent à comprendre la nécessité de travailler en mode projet. Toutefois, cette évolution doit s’accompagner de modèles économiques viables.
Pour Mawndoé Célestin, la presse ne doit donc pas seulement être sollicitée pour assurer la visibilité des initiatives culturelles. Elle peut aussi contribuer à poser les bonnes questions, à analyser les réalités du marché et à faire émerger des pistes de réflexion.  « On ne peut pas exister socialement si on n’existe pas économiquement »,  a-t-il soutenu, résumant ainsi l’un des défis majeurs auxquels les artistes tchadiens sont confrontés. La rencontre a ainsi été présentée comme un cadre d’échange appelé à se renouveler, avec l’ambition de faire émerger des débats et, éventuellement, des actions de plaidoyer en faveur du secteur culturel.

Sénégal : Au moins 21 morts dans le naufrage d’une pirogue de migrants
admin
novembre 8, 2026
1 minutes de lecture
63 vues
Au moins 21 personnes ont péri dans le naufrage d’une pirogue transportant des migrants au large de Kébémer, dans le nord-ouest du Sénégal. Le bilan provisoire, communiqué samedi 7 novembre 2026 par le ministère sénégalais de l’Intérieur, fait également état d’un seul rescapé.
Selon les autorités, les opérations de recherche se poursuivent afin de retrouver d’éventuels survivants et de porter assistance aux familles des victimes.
Ce drame intervient dans un contexte marqué par les tentatives répétées de traversées clandestines de l’Atlantique.
Chaque année, des milliers de migrants, majoritairement des jeunes originaires d’Afrique de l’Ouest, prennent la mer à bord d’embarcations souvent surchargées et vétustes, dans l’espoir de rejoindre l’Europe, notamment les îles Canaries.

admin
novembre 8, 2026
1 minutes de lecture

Le maire de la ville de N’Djamena, Sénoussi Hassana Abdoulaye, a reçu une délégation de l’Union européenne au Tchad, conduite par son ambassadeur, Amador Sanchez Rico, à la Maison des Bénévoles.
Au cours de cette rencontre, le maire et ses équipes ont présenté la feuille de route de la Commune ainsi que dix projets structurants destinés à accompagner la transformation de la capitale. Les discussions ont porté sur les priorités municipales, le développement urbain et l’amélioration du cadre de vie des populations.
La séance de travail a été suivie d’une visite de terrain à la Maison de quartier et à la Place à vivre de Chagoua, permettant à la délégation européenne de découvrir ces infrastructures de proximité et les initiatives mises en œuvre au profit des habitants.
À travers cette rencontre, la Commune de N’Djamena entend renforcer ses relations avec l’Union européenne et explorer de nouvelles possibilités de partenariat pour soutenir des projets concrets en faveur d’une capitale plus moderne, inclusive et durable.

La sénatrice Djenom Moguena Micheline a rendu hommage à feu Sa Majesté Aarong Abdoul Banda, ancien chef de canton de Deresia, décédé le 16 octobre 2026.
Dans son témoignage, elle a salué le parcours du défunt, qui a consacré plus de 33 ans au service de sa communauté à la tête de la chefferie cantonale. Elle a également exprimé son soutien à sa famille biologique en cette période de deuil.

original_payload.original_title: Semaine culturelle : Une conférence pour briser le tabou autour du cancer de la prostate
original_payload.original_body:
Semaine culturelle : Une conférence pour briser le tabou autour du cancer de la prostate
admin
novembre 8, 2026
1 minutes de lecture
142 vues
Dans le cadre de la deuxième édition de la Semaine culturelle de la Commune du 1er arrondissement de N’Djamena, une conférence-débat consacrée au cancer de la prostate s’est tenue ce samedi 7 novembre 2026.
Animée par le Dr Lytagoto, elle était placée sous le thème : «  Le cancer de la prostate : au-delà du tabou, un mal qui peut être guéri  ».
Au cours des échanges, le médecin a sensibilisé les participants sur cette maladie qui reste encore entourée de nombreux préjugés. Il a notamment insisté sur l’importance de mieux s’informer, de consulter un professionnel de santé et de ne pas négliger le dépistage.
À travers cette initiative, les organisateurs souhaitent profiter de la Semaine culturelle pour aborder des sujets qui touchent directement la vie des populations.
L’occasion d’encourager les hommes à briser le silence autour du cancer de la prostate et à prendre soin de leur santé.

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : Abakar Police, de figure emblématique de la circulation à une situation de détresse à Klessoum
original_payload.original_body:
Longtemps connu des usagers de la route pour son engagement dans la régulation de la circulation aux principaux carrefours de N’Djaména, le commandant de la Police nationale, Abakar Zeïd, surnommé « Abakar Police », se retrouve aujourd’hui dans une situation préoccupante.
Rencontré ce dimanche 8 novembre 2026 à Klessoum, où il vit désormais auprès de sa famille, l’ancien agent de terrain témoigne des difficultés auxquelles il est confronté depuis son retour d’une évacuation sanitaire en Égypte.
Évacué le 25 juillet 2025 sur instruction du Premier ministre, Allah-Maye Halina, Abakar Police y a bénéficié de trois mois de soins médicaux avant de regagner le Tchad le 28 octobre de la même année.
Dans son témoignage, il évoque notamment le sentiment d’abandon et les conditions difficiles dans lesquelles il affirme vivre actuellement.

items.title: Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final to Claire Liu in straight sets

original_payload.original_title: Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final to Claire Liu in straight sets
original_payload.original_body:
Tennis trailblazer Alex Eala from the Philippines burst into tears as she reflected on a “life-changing” season after falling agonisingly short of a second WTA Tour title in Hong Kong.
The second seed was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Claire Liu in the final of the Hong Kong Open as the American, ranked 102nd, won her first tour title on Sunday.
Recommended Stories

list 3 of 3  Bergs stuns Alcaraz in Shanghai as Zverev claims year’s top tennis ranking
end of list
Eala is at a career-high 17 in the world after a breakout year in which the 21-year-old clinched her maiden title, in Washington, DC, in August.
That victory made her the first player from the Philippines to win a tournament on the WTA Tour.
Eala, set to rise to world number 15 next week, started the year ranked 50th.
“This season has changed my life; it’s changed my life for the better,” Eala, who finished the final with heavy strapping on her right leg, told the crowd afterwards.
Becoming emotional as she addressed her team in the stands, she said: “I’m incredibly proud of the work we’ve put in this year.
“We’re the only ones that truly know what it took to arrive to this point in our journey.
“This is only the beginning.”

original_payload.original_body:
A small boat carrying migrants and refugees has sunk off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 21 people.
The Senegalese Interior Ministry said in a statement on Sunday that one person had been rescued in addition to the 21 bodies recovered.

The ministry said the death toll was “provisional” as of late Saturday, adding that the search was still ongoing and the families of the victims were being helped.
Media reports said the pirogue-type flat-bottomed boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in the Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.
Le Soleil newspaper said that most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.
Thousands ⁠of people have ⁠died in recent years attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands from West Africa, including ‌635 in the first five months of this year, according to ‌migrant rights ‌group Walking Borders
Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro  declared  an emergency on Saturday after a surge in migrant boat arrivals. Since the start of November, El Hierro authorities said more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard around 30 boats.

items.title: Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya

original_payload.original_title: Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya
original_payload.original_body:
The reopening of the Egyptian embassy in Tripoli marks a fundamental political shift, both domestically and regionally, for Libya, analysts say.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty inaugurated the historic embassy building on Saturday, which had been closed for 12 years due to security concerns.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Why has the Libya-Turkiye maritime deal stirred controversy?
list 2 of 3  Saddam Haftar is eyeing the throne in Libya
list 3 of 3  Can Turkiye’s Libya breakthrough reshape Eastern Mediterranean diplomacy?
end of list
Libya has been politically divided since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, with rival administrations formed in Tripoli in the west and Tobruk and Benghazi in the east.
Egypt was widely considered to be backing the eastern authority, effectively led by strongman and renegade military commander Khalifa Haftar, and his self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA), until recent regional developments led Cairo to rethink its approach.
Libyan political analyst Hazem al-Rayes said the reopening of the embassy in Tripoli – which was the seat of the internationally recognised government that Haftar was fighting – is a sign of this.
“I can consider that what Egypt is doing in its recent moves towards the capital, Tripoli, is an attempt to readjust its behaviour in the Libyan file … [for] five years, no Egyptian foreign minister visited the capital,” he told Al Jazeera.
Elias al-Barouni, a political science professor at Libya’s Nalut University, also believes the move goes beyond the resumption of regular consular services in Tripoli.
“We are facing an indicator of a shift in Cairo’s method of managing its relations with the Libyan parties, and a rearrangement of its priorities in dealing with the Libyan crisis,” al-Barouni told Al Jazeera.
original_payload.original_summary: Former rivals in Libya are pushing for a unity government to end years of conflict.
original_payload.author: Mohammad Mansour

items.title: Could Iraq’s Kurdish region return to two separate administrations?

original_payload.original_title: Could Iraq’s Kurdish region return to two separate administrations?
original_payload.original_body:
Disagreements between the  Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK)  over the formation of a new government have led to the threat of two rival administrations emerging in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, analysts say.
The dispute between the two dominant political forces in the semiautonomous Kurdistan Regional Government, which traditionally has operated under a power-sharing agreement, escalated after a parliamentary session was held last week in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  Iraq’s Shia bloc divided over tactics after US rejects al-Maliki for PM
list 3 of 3  Iraq’s Kurdish forces look to a new era after US withdrawal
end of list
PUK leader  Bafel Talabani  responded by withdrawing his party from the government, and a threat is growing that a rival administration could be formed in the party’s Sulaimaniyah base.
Independent Kurdish politician Yasin Aziz said the latest developments have deepened the historical divisions between the KDP and PUK.
“I believe the spectre of two administrations in Kurdistan is now very close, and the outlines of such a scenario are becoming clear. … The events have been painful and rapid. The differences between the two parties were significant and have now led to a breakdown in relations,” Aziz told Al Jazeera.
“There had been hopes that the two sides would reach an agreement, but activating parliament without the PUK deepened the divisions between the KDP and PUK.”
The KDP, which is led by Massoud Barzani, is the biggest party in the region, and its strongholds are in Erbil and Dohuk.
Masrour Barzani welcomes KDP President Masoud Barzani at the Middle East Peace and Security Forum (MEPS) in Duhok, Iraq on 18 November 2025 [Ismael Adnan/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images]   Two powers
Since the first Gulf War in 1990 and 1991 and the establishment of a US-led “no-fly zone” in northern Iraq, Iraq’s Kurds have largely governed themselves, separate from the national government in Baghdad.

items.title: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe

original_payload.original_title: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe
original_payload.original_body:
Poland has begun two days of national mourning after an armed man killed six people in central Krakow, as the national prosecutor’s office opened a “terrorism” investigation.
The 24-year-old Polish suspect opened fire on Saturday in the heart of Krakow’s historic city centre. A British national was among those killed, according to police, and nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia were among the 15 wounded, authorities told the PAP news agency.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Three injured in third school attack in Poland in less than a week
list 2 of 3  Polish president holds crisis talks in court standoff
list 3 of 3  At least six people killed in shooting in Poland’s Krakow main square
end of list
Three more bodies were later found at the suspect’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 150km (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.
The suspect was also wounded during police action and is in critical condition in hospital.
Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said on social media on Sunday it had “launched an investigation today into yesterday’s attack in Krakow”, adding it was probing “the killing of six people … using a firearm, and the attempted murder of many others, including police officers, this act constituting a terrorist offence”.
Daniel Prokopowicz, a spokesperson for the office, said it was “highly likely” that the killings in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski and Krakow were carried out by the same person, but that investigations were ongoing.
According to media reports, the suspect, Michal O, had a valid gun licence and no prior criminal record.
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski stated the attacker was influenced by far-right and ultranationalist ideologies and views.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity

original_payload.original_title: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity
original_payload.original_body:
More than 600,000 people in Ukraine’s eastern Dnipropetrovsk region are without electricity after a Russian overnight attack on an energy facility, a Ukrainian energy provider has said.
Residents across the Pavlohrad, Samarivskyi, Kamianske and Dnipro districts, as well as the city of Dnipro, faced electricity outages on Sunday, power company DTEK wrote in a Telegram post.

list 2 of 3  Zelenskyy accuses Russia of escalating strikes ahead of peace talks
list 3 of 3  ‘They started bombing us with drones’: Russian attacks unnerve Zaporizhzhia
end of list
Engineers were at the scene attempting to restore the damaged facility, but “repairs are being complicated by repeated attacks”, DTEK said.
Ukraine is bracing for yet another harsh winter of war as Russia ramps up daily aerial attacks, raining down drones and missiles on the power network.
Another 250,000 Ukrainians were left without power in the Kharkiv region in northeastern Ukraine on Sunday after Russia struck an infrastructure facility there.
“No casualties have been reported, ” said Mykola Baksheyev, mayor of Zlatopil city, on Telegram.
“Power engineers are currently working to repair the damage; however, the exact timeframe for restoring the electricity supply remains unknown.”
The attacks came a day after Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy said a massive attack on energy facilities had plunged residents in five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying attacks to put pressure on Kyiv at United States-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.
Russia’s Ministry of Defence stated on its Telegram channel that its forces will “continue to carry out strikes against Ukrainian fuel and energy infrastructure facilities” that they say are used to aid the Ukrainian military.

items.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections

original_payload.original_title: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
original_payload.original_body:
South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments.
With 99 percent of the votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had 31 percent nationally against 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA).
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh damaged in ‘attempted’ attack
list 3 of 3  Ukraine’s position ‘may become stronger’ as US Democrats regain some power
end of list
That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance.
Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties.
Final results are expected to be announced at 6pm (16:00 GMT) on Sunday.
While still the largest party in South Africa, the ANC’s support has steadily eroded as voters grow increasingly frustrated with corruption and the party’s failure to tackle unemployment, which tops 34 percent more than three decades after the end of apartheid.
Failures in basic services, such as water and electricity, have also contributed to the ANC’s vote share falling in local elections over the past 15 years.
The party failed to win an outright majority in any of the eight major metro areas, including Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Helen Zille, the Democratic Alliance’s mayoral candidate for Johannesburg, speaks at the party’s final campaign rally in Mamelodi, east of Pretoria, on October 31, 2026 [Ilaria Finizio/AFP]   Coalition talks
Since no party won more than 50 percent of the votes in many cities, including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up or hash it out with smaller parties to form municipal governments.

items.title: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?

original_payload.original_title: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
original_payload.original_body:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been given the opportunity to  form a new government  after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections, raising the possibility of an end to his long tenure in power.
President Isaac Herzog selected the former military chief on Saturday, following consultations with political parties. Eisenkot has 28 days to cobble together a coalition to form a government. If he fails to form a new administration within that period, he can seek a 14-day extension.

end of list
“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, posted on X.
However, the 66-year-old faces a difficult challenge as many of the opposition parties hold sharply conflicting positions on national security, religion and the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has a 61-seat majority in Israel’s 120-member parliament, the Knesset.
As a result, Arab-led parties hold a potentially decisive role in determining who governs Israel, even as Eisenkot and his prospective partners refuse to rely on their support.
So what do we now know about Eisenkot’s possible paths to power, and can he succeed in unseating Netanyahu?
Can Eisenkot unite Israel’s divided opposition?
Eisenkot’s potential coalition spans his Yashar party, the centre-left Democrats led by Yair Golan, Naftali Bennett’s centre-right Together party and Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu (Israel Our Home).

original_payload.original_body: Selon l'OMS, l'Afrique supporte une part importante et disproportionnée de la charge mondiale du paludisme. En 2024, 95% des cas de paludisme sur une population de 265 millions ont été enregistrés en Afrique. La même année, 579.000 personnes sur le continent dont plus de la moitié sont des enfants y ont succombés, ajoute l'agence onusienne. Paradoxalement, les progrès dans la lutte sont étouffés par plusieurs contraintes. Malgré la volonté politique et l'expertise scientifique, la lutte à l'échelle continentale se heurte à l'insuffisance de ressources financières et logistiques, soulignent les chercheurs du centre scientifique de parasitologie de l'Institut Pasteur de Dakar. Selon le Dr Niang, le responsable du centre, « les quatre pays africains ayant jusque-là obtenus la certification de l'OMS combinent une géographie gérable, avec d'un côté des villes insulaires et de l'autre des zones fortement désertiques ; facilitant la surveillance et le contrôle de la transmission : c'est le cas du Cap-Vert et de l'Île Maurice, par exemple. A l'inverse, le climat dans les pays subsahariens comme le Nigéria, la République démocratique du Congo, entre autres, favorise une transmission continue pratiquement toute l'année et la taille de la population pose une contrainte budgétaire majeure. » Il faut tout de même rester optimiste à la vue des résultats obtenus ces dernières années sur le continent, assure Makhtar Niang qui rappelle avoir travaillé avec beaucoup de pays dont le Sénégal sur un plan d'élimination du paludisme d'ici à 2030. Face à l'asymétrie des ressources financières et logistiques, les dirigeants africains devraient investir une partie importante des finances publiques dans l'élimination des obstacles inhérents à la lutte contre le paludisme tout en renforçant la solidarité régionale face à la maladie.
original_payload.original_summary: La Guinée équatoriale intensifie sa lutte contre le paludisme avec l’objectif de l’éradiquer dans les prochaines années grâce à la vaccination, aux insecticides et à de nouvelles technologies. Les autorités y voient un levier essentiel pour accélérer le développement économique du pays.

items.title: Racisme et inégalités de genre à l’ONU : Guterres reconnaît des progrès insuffisants

original_payload.original_title: Racisme et inégalités de genre à l’ONU : Guterres reconnaît des progrès insuffisants
original_payload.original_body:
Six ans après une enquête interne révélant qu’un fonctionnaire de l’ONU sur trois déclarait avoir subi une discrimination raciale, le secrétaire général António Guterres a reconnu, ce mercredi 28 octobre, que les avancées contre le racisme et les inégalités entre les sexes au sein de l’Organisation restent insuffisantes.
« L’ONU ne peut défendre de manière crédible l’égalité dans le monde si nous ne la faisons pas respecter à l’intérieur de nos propres murs », a déclaré M. Guterres devant ses collaborateurs réunis dans la salle du Conseil économique et social (ECOSOC).
Les chiffres de l’enquête de 2020 avaient été établis à la suite du meurtre de George Floyd aux États-Unis, qui avait déclenché une vague mondiale de mobilisations contre le racisme. « C’était totalement inacceptable », a reconnu le chef de l’ONU. L’Organisation avait alors admis qu’il ne suffisait plus de condamner le racisme : il fallait devenir « activement antiraciste ».
Depuis, un groupe de travail a été créé, des formations obligatoires ont été mises en place et une collecte volontaire de données raciales a été engagée. Pourtant, selon le secrétaire général, la diversité du personnel ne se traduit pas forcément à tous les niveaux de la hiérarchie. « L’inégalité entre les sexes est une question de pouvoir. Le racisme est une question de pouvoir. Et le pouvoir n’est jamais donné, il se prend », a-t-il insisté.
Sur la parité, des progrès plus marquants ont été enregistrés. L’ONU a atteint la parité dans les postes de direction et parmi le personnel de la catégorie des administrateurs. « Nous y sommes parvenus non pas en abaissant les exigences, mais en multipliant les possibilités », a souligné M. Guterres. « Mais la parité n’est pas la ligne d’arrivée. »
Lire aussi  :  ”Il faudra encore 171 ans pour atteindre l’égalité des sexes“, selon l’ONU
Les femmes doivent encore pouvoir influencer réellement les décisions, progresser dans leur carrière et travailler à l’abri des violences et du harcèlement.
Ces acquis sont aujourd’hui menacés par la crise financière que traverse l’Organisation. Face aux retards de paiement de plusieurs États membres, la réforme « ONU80 » prévoit une réduction de 21 % des postes au Secrétariat en 2026.
Le secrétaire général a appelé à protéger les avancées en matière d’égalité des sexes, à maintenir la lutte contre le racisme parmi les priorités et à garantir des recrutements et des promotions transparents, exempts de préjugés. « Nous devons résister au recul des droits, en commençant chez nous », a-t-il conclu.

items.title: Climat : la chaleur a causé un record de 710 000 décès dans le monde en 2023

original_payload.original_title: Climat : la chaleur a causé un record de 710 000 décès dans le monde en 2023
original_payload.original_body:
La chaleur a été associée à un nombre record de 710 000 décès estimés dans le monde en 2023, selon le 10e rapport Lancet Countdown sur la santé et le changement climatique, publié mercredi 28 octobre 2026.
Pour la première fois, 71,5 % de ces décès sont imputables au réchauffement d’origine humaine, indique l’étude réalisée en partenariat avec l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS).
Ce bilan dépasse celui du paludisme ou du VIH pour la même année. Entre 2016 et 2023, la chaleur a été liée en moyenne à 540 800 décès par an, dont 68 % (environ 369 900) attribués au changement climatique. C’est une nette hausse par rapport à la décennie 2006-2015, où cette part n’était que de 55 %.
Au total, le changement climatique est estimé avoir causé près de 3 millions de décès liés à la chaleur entre 2016 et 2023. La moyenne annuelle des décès liés à la chaleur a augmenté de près de 36 % depuis l’entrée en vigueur de l’Accord de Paris.
Les personnes âgées, les femmes et les personnes souffrant de pathologies préexistantes sont particulièrement vulnérables. La chaleur aggrave notamment les maladies cardiovasculaires, les insuffisances rénales et le risque de décès prématuré.
Lire aussi  :  Réchauffement climatique : la chaleur extrême ferait vieillir plus vite
Le rapport appelle les gouvernements et les organisations internationales à reconnaître formellement le changement climatique comme une « urgence sanitaire mondiale »
« Les atteintes à la santé progressent plus rapidement que la réponse mondiale, malgré des avancées dans les investissements en énergies propres », a souligné Marina Romanello, directrice exécutive du Lancet Countdown.
D’autres indicateurs confirment l’aggravation : en 2025, près de 52 % des terres mondiales ont connu au moins un mois de sécheresse extrême, l’un des niveaux les plus élevés jamais enregistrés. La chaleur a également réduit la capacité de travail, entraînant des pertes économiques estimées à plus de 1 000 milliards de dollars en 2025.
Le Lancet Countdown, collaboration internationale basée à l’University College London, suit depuis dix ans les liens entre climat et santé. Ses auteurs insistent sur la nécessité de placer la protection de la santé au cœur des politiques climatiques et de financer l’adaptation, en particulier dans les pays les plus vulnérables.

original_payload.original_title: Au moins 21 morts dans le naufrage d’une pirogue de migrants au Sénégal
original_payload.original_body:

Samedi également, la gendarmerie sénégalaise a annoncé avoir intercepté au large de Dakar 142 migrants clandestins, dont plusieurs femmes et des enfants, qui tentaient de rejoindre l’Espagne à bord d’une pirogue.
Des milliers de personnes sont mortes ou ont disparu en tentant de rejoindre ainsi l’Europe ces dernières années.

items.title: Au large du Sénégal, au moins 21 personnes sont mortes dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants

original_payload.original_title: Au large du Sénégal, au moins 21 personnes sont mortes dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants
original_payload.original_body:
Le bilan est provisoire. Au 21 personnes sont mortes dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants au large de Kébémer, dans le nord-ouest du  Sénégal  où, selon les autorités, les recherches d'éventuels survivants se poursuivent.
Des milliers de personnes originaires d' Afrique  de l'Ouest, en majorité des jeunes, tentent depuis des années de gagner clandestinement l' Europe  en empruntant la route de l'Atlantique, principalement vers l'archipel espagnol des Canaries, à bord d'embarcations surchargées, souvent vétustes.
"Au soir du 7 novembre 2026, le bilan provisoire fait état de 21 corps sans vie et d’un rescapé", a indiqué le ministère sénégalais de l'Intérieur dans un communiqué, sans préciser le jour du naufrage.
À lire aussi  "Leur absence pèse chaque minute" : au Sénégal, le deuil impossible des proches de migrants disparus
"Les services compétents de l’État sont mobilisés pour poursuivre les recherches, porter secours aux éventuels rescapés et accompagner les familles", a-t-il ajouté.
La "compassion et la solidarité de l'État"
Le ministre de l'Intérieur doit se rendre sur les lieux lundi pour "témoigner aux familles des victimes et aux populations affectées la compassion et la solidarité de l’État", selon le communiqué.
"Le naufrage s'est produit vendredi", a déclaré à l'AFP Saliou Diouf, fondateur de "Boza Fii", l'une des principales associations d'aide aux personnes migrantes au Sénégal.
Selon le quotidien national Le Soleil, le drame a eu lieu au large des côtes de la localité de Loumpoul, dans la région de Louga (département de Kébémer), entre Dakar et Saint-Louis.
"La plupart des victimes seraient originaires des communes de Léona et de Thiéppe", dans le même département, ajoute le quotidien.
"On ne sait pas exactement s'il y a d'autres nationalités car les recherches se poursuivent. Mais les corps repêchés hier (samedi) sont ceux de Sénégalais", a précisé Saliou Diouf.
À voir aussi  Sénégal : les migrants, fantômes de l'Atlantique
Une pirogue interceptée avec 142 personnes
Samedi également, la gendarmerie sénégalaise a annoncé avoir intercepté au large de Dakar 142 migrants clandestins, dont des femmes et des enfants, qui tentaient de rejoindre l' Espagne  à bord d'une pirogue.
L'opération a eu lieu vendredi et a été menée "en marge de la couverture sécuritaire" des  Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar , le tout premier événement olympique à se dérouler sur le sol africain.
Parmi les personnes interceptées figurent 40 Sénégalais dont quatre femmes, 93 Gambiens dont 17 femmes, un ressortissant de  Guinée-Bissau , deux Guinéens et deux Nigérians, selon la gendarmerie.
Le groupe comptait également deux nourrissons et deux enfants mineurs, ajoute-t-elle.
À voir aussi  Sénégal : le "deuil invisible" des enfants de migrants disparus en mer
Les réseaux de passeurs dans le collimateur
Fuyant les conflits qui ravagent leur pays, comme le  Mali , l'autoritarisme des juntes, ou la pauvreté et le manque d'opportunités, des milliers de jeunes Ouest-Africains tentent depuis des années d'émigrer, notamment vers l'Europe.
Des milliers de personnes sont mortes ou ont disparu en tentant de rejoindre ainsi l'Europe ces dernières années.
Fin octobre, l'ONG Action pour les droits humains et l'amitié (ADHA) avait interpellé le Sénégal sur la persistance de "départs dangereux" vers l'Europe de migrants, dont "près de 1 000"  Ouest-Africains arrivés aux Canaries espagnoles  les 22 et 23 octobre.
"Le gouvernement réaffirme sa détermination à combattre les réseaux de passeurs, notamment par une coopération renforcée avec les pays voisins", a souligné le ministère de l'Intérieur dans son communiqué.
original_payload.original_summary: Au moins 21 personnes ont péri dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants au large de Kébémer, dans le nord-ouest du Sénégal, ont annoncé dimanche les autorités. Selon le ministère de l'Intérieur, un seul rescapé a été retrouvé et les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver d'éventuels survivants.

items.title: JOJ- Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal s’offre ses premières médailles d’or

original_payload.original_title: JOJ- Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal s’offre ses premières médailles d’or
original_payload.original_body:
Le Sénégal a décroché ses deux premières médailles d’or aux 4es Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), grâce à Elisabeth Diatta et Maguette Diop, le 7 novembre 2026, lors de la 7 e  journée. Selon la chaine publique (RTS), Elisabeth Diatta est sacrée championne en lutte de plage dans la catégorie des moins de 55 kg, alors Maguette Diop, lui, a été sacré champion dans la catégorie homme des 80 Kg de la même discipline.
La jeune lutteuse a dominé en finale la Japonaise Reisa Kojima. Quant à Maguette Diop âgé de 16 ans il s’est défait de l’Azerbaïdjanais, Nihad Suleymanli sur le score de 4 à 0, selon le média public.  Tous les deux athlètes ont inscrit ainsi leur nom au palmarès de cette quatrième édition de l’événement.
Performante tout au long de la compétition, Elisabeth Diatta a confirmé sa montée en puissance dans l’épreuve décisive. Son titre a permis au Sénégal d’ouvrir son compteur de médailles dorées devant son public, avant d’être suivi par Maguette Diop, pour le doublé dans la même journée.
Maguette Diop lui, est resté invaincu tout au long de la compétition : trois victoires en poule, puis une demi-finale gagnée contre l’Iranien Reza Jalilian, selon l’Agence de presse sénégalaise (APS)
Ces deux médailles d’or ainsi que le bronze remporté le 1 er  novembre en Judo par Matar Diop (-66 kg),contre le Français Nathan Gbingbehi, ont permis au Sénégal de monter à la 10e place du classement général, après sept journées de compétition.
Le bilan du Sénégal peut évoluer ce 8 novembre 2026 à l’issue d’autres finales de lutte de plage. Il s’agit des 70 kg et 90 kg (homme), et 45 kg et 65 kg (femme).

items.title: 2027: Ekiti REC seeks stakeholders’ support for credible polls

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Ekiti REC seeks stakeholders’ support for credible polls
original_payload.original_body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has expressed readiness for the conduct of the 2027 general elections in Ekiti State.
The state Resident Electoral Commissioner, Dr Bunmi Omoseyindemi, urged election stakeholders in the state to collaborate and play their parts to ensure a successful exercise.

Claire Liu a remporté son premier titre en simple sur le circuit WTA, dimanche 8 novembre à Hong Kong. L’Américaine, 102e mondiale, a battu la Philippine Alexandra Eala, tête de série numéro 2, en deux sets, 6-3, 6-0.
La finale est restée équilibrée jusqu’à 3-3 dans la première manche, chacune des deux joueuses ayant déjà pris une fois le service adverse. Liu a ensuite enchaîné neuf jeux pour conclure en une heure et trente-trois minutes.
Ce succès achève une semaine sans le moindre set concédé pour l’Américaine. Avant Eala, elle avait écarté Tatiana Prozorova, Katie Boulter, Zeynep Sonmez et Alexandra Shubladze, à chaque fois en deux manches.
Liu disputait seulement son septième tableau principal de la saison sur le circuit WTA. Classée 221e au début de l’année, elle doit retrouver le top 70 au prochain classement. Son meilleur rang reste une 52e place, atteinte en janvier 2023.
Eala jouait, elle, sa troisième finale en simple sur ce circuit. Déjà titrée à Washington en août, elle manque l’occasion de décrocher un deuxième trophée. Liu l’avait également battue lors de leur première rencontre, au premier tour du tournoi de Guangzhou en 2025.

40 000 fidèles à Paysandú avant la veillée
Près de 100 000 personnes se sont rassemblées samedi 7 novembre 2026 au stade Centenario de Montevideo et à ses abords pour la veillée de prière présidée par le pape Léon XIV, selon un bilan des autorités locales rapporté par Vatican News.
Environ 70 000 fidèles ont suivi la cérémonie à l’intérieur du stade, tandis que 30 000 autres y ont participé depuis les alentours, où des écrans géants avaient été installés. La foule a accueilli le souverain pontife par des chants après plusieurs heures d’attente dans les rues voisines.
Devant les participants, Léon XIV a appelé les catholiques à témoigner de leur foi dans une société marquée par la sécularisation. S’adressant particulièrement aux jeunes, il les a encouragés à ne pas craindre les engagements durables, notamment le mariage et la vie familiale.
40 000 fidèles à Paysandú avant la veillée
Plus tôt dans la journée, le pape avait célébré à Paysandú sa première messe de ce voyage en Amérique du Sud. Quelque 40 000 personnes, venues également d’Argentine et du Brésil, y ont assisté malgré la pluie. Dans son homélie, il a évoqué le pont qui relie les rives uruguayenne et argentine du fleuve Uruguay pour inviter les populations à dépasser leurs divisions.
À Montevideo, Léon XIV s’est aussi rendu dans le quartier de Casavalle, où il a rencontré des habitants et des acteurs associatifs engagés dans l’accès au logement, l’accompagnement des personnes dépendantes et l’insertion professionnelle. Il a appelé à ne pas détourner le regard de la pauvreté et des inégalités.
Le souverain pontife doit achever dimanche 8 novembre son séjour en Uruguay par une messe à Florida, avant de s’envoler dans l’après-midi pour Buenos Aires. L’Argentine constitue la deuxième étape de son voyage, qui doit ensuite se poursuivre au Pérou jusqu’au 17 novembre.

Le ministère égyptien du Pétrole a annoncé, vendredi 6 novembre, des résultats positifs pour le puits exploratoire Nasim-1X, dans la concession de Tiba, en Méditerranée. Ses premières estimations font état d’environ 200 milliards de pieds cubes de gaz dans le réservoir, soit près de 5,7 milliards de mètres cubes.
Cette estimation ne correspond pas encore à un volume commercialement récupérable. Les études techniques se poursuivent pour évaluer les quantités pouvant être produites, les débits envisageables et la viabilité commerciale du gisement. Aucune date de mise en production n’a été annoncée.
Le forage a mis en évidence une épaisseur nette de couche contenant du gaz d’environ 15 mètres. La concession est exploitée par le groupe italien Eni en partenariat avec l’australien Woodside. Petrobel a réalisé les opérations de forage pour leur compte.
Pour accélérer le développement de la découverte, les autorités prévoient une conduite d’environ 22 kilomètres vers le gazoduc Abu Madi-El Gamil. Ce raccordement permettrait d’utiliser des installations déjà en place et de raccourcir le délai nécessaire au démarrage de la production.
L’Égypte cherche à relever sa production nationale après plusieurs années de recul qui ont accru sa dépendance aux importations de gaz. La demande des centrales électriques et de l’industrie donne un enjeu concret au développement de nouveaux puits, même si la contribution de Nasim-1X reste à établir.

Le gouvernement britannique envisage d’inclure Vinted et eBay dans l’interdiction d’accès aux plateformes en ligne destinée aux moins de 16 ans. La ministre de la Culture, Lisa Nandy, a confirmé dimanche 8 novembre que cette possibilité était sérieusement étudiée pour protéger les enfants.
Interrogée sur la BBC, la ministre n’a pas annoncé de décision définitive concernant ces deux sites de vente. Annoncé en juin 2026, le dispositif britannique visant les réseaux sociaux doit entrer en vigueur en mars 2027 et concerner notamment Instagram, TikTok et Snapchat.
eBay indique déjà réserver l’inscription aux personnes de plus de 18 ans, les transactions impliquant la conclusion d’un contrat. Vinted fixe également un âge minimal de 18 ans pour ses utilisateurs. eBay s’est dit disposé à poursuivre les échanges avec le gouvernement, tout en soulignant que les détails du projet restaient à clarifier.
Le gouvernement n’a pas encore publié la liste complète des services visés. Certaines fonctions permettant à des inconnus de contacter des enfants, dont les messageries de sites de jeux, doivent aussi être restreintes. Une restriction de ces fonctions ne signifie donc pas nécessairement l’interdiction de tout le service.
Cette démarche britannique intervient après  l’entrée en vigueur de l’interdiction australienne en décembre 2025 .

Novartis fait état de neuf signalements depuis 2019. Dans deux dossiers, le matériel génétique utilisé pour administrer le traitement a été retrouvé dans les cellules tumorales.
Santé      Par  Parfait Nougbotin
